title: Combined pronouns: me lo, te la, glielo, ce ne
rule: When an indirect and a direct pronoun (or ne) meet, the indirect comes first and changes: mi → me, ti → te, ci → ce, vi → ve, si → se; gli and le (and Le) both become glie- and fuse with the second pronoun: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele, gliene. The pair goes before the conjugated verb (glielo dico), attaches as one word to infinitives, gerunds, ecco and tu / noi / voi imperatives (dirglielo, dammelo, eccotelo), and goes before the Lei imperative (me lo dia). With modals, either position. The participle agrees with the direct pronoun (gliel'ho data, me le hanno rubate). Ci (there) + ne = ce ne (ce ne sono tre).

head: + lo
+ la
+ li
+ le
+ ne
blocks.note: Glie- is the same for to him, to her, to you (formal) and to them. Context tells you which. In careful writing, "to them" can be lo… loro (lo dico loro), but nobody says it.

rows: Glielo dico. Non glielo dico. Me l'ha dato.
I tell him. I don't tell him. He gave it to me.
I'd like to tell him. Before giving it to him…
Give it to me. Tell him. Bring me two. Tell me.
Let's tell him. Bring it (f.) to me.
Non dirmelo. / Non me lo dire.
Me lo dia. Glielo dica. Non me lo dica.
Give it to me. Tell him. Don't tell me.
Here it is for you. Here it is for him. Here are two for me.
Me lo metto. Se la prende. Me ne vado.
I put it on. He takes it. I'm leaving.
Gliel'ho data. Me le hanno rubate. Ce ne hanno portate tre.
I gave it (f.) to her. They stole them (f.) from me. They brought us three.

items.t: La bici per il nipote? Gliela ordino, gliela sistemo, gliela consegno a casa.
items.n: The bike for the grandson? I'll order it for her, fix it up for her, deliver it to her house.

items.t: Il modulo me lo riporti lunedì. Le marche da bollo gliele vendo io, se vuole.
items.n: The form, bring it back to me on Monday. The revenue stamps, I'll sell them to you, if you like.

items.t: Te lo prometto: non glielo dico a Pasquale. Diglielo tu, se hai coraggio.
items.n: I promise you: I won't tell Pasquale. You tell him, if you dare.

items.t: Chiavi? Ce ne sono tre. Caffè? Nando ce lo porta. Birre? Ce le ha già segnate.
items.n: Spanners? There are three. Coffee? Nando brings it to us. Beers? He's already put them on our tab.

blocks.title: Build it in two steps
blocks.text: First find the indirect pronoun (to whom?): [[gli]]. Then the direct (what?): [[la]]. Put them together, change the first: [[gliela]]. Mi + lo: [[me lo]]. Ci + ne: [[ce ne]]. Then place the pair exactly where a single pronoun would go. Say it as one unstressed sound before the verb: [[glielo-DIco]].

items.wrong: Mi lo dà. Ti la cambio. Ci ne sono.
items.right: Me lo dà. Te la cambio. Ce ne sono.
items.why: i → e before the second pronoun.

items.wrong: Gli lo dico. Le la ordino. Gli ne do.
items.right: Glielo dico. Gliela ordino. Gliene do.

items.wrong: Lo me dà. La ti cambio.
items.right: Me lo dà. Te la cambio.

items.wrong: Dire glielo. Da me lo. Ecco te lo.
items.why: One word when attached; dammelo doubles the m after da'.

items.wrong: Gliel'ho dato (la bici). Me le ha dato (le chiavi).
items.right: Gliel'ho data. Me le ha date.

items.q: Le chiavi? Dora ___ ___ ha date. (to me + them) Il preventivo? ___ ___ mando stasera. (to you, formal + it) La verità? ___ ___ dico io, a Pasquale. (to him + it) Le birre? Nando ___ ___ ha segnate. (to us + them)
items.n: The keys? Dora gave them to me. The quote? I'll send it to you tonight. The truth? I'll tell Pasquale myself. The beers? Nando put them on our tab.
items.hint: for the quote and the truth, the second blank is the verb

items.q: «Bring it to me!» (to a friend; it = il modulo)
items.why: porta + me + lo, one word, indirect first.

items.q: I'll give it to you tomorrow, I promise. (to a friend; it = il permesso)
answers: Te lo do domani, te lo prometto
Te lo darò domani, te lo prometto
